quests.title: The Garrison Blood Debt
quests.synopsis: Colonel Harven sends notice: one of your survivors, former conscript Ola Vask, is listed as a deserter under military law. Surrender her or face supply embargo.

stages.title: The Colonel's Notice
stages.narrativePrompt: A garrison courier delivers a wax-sealed tri-fold. Inside: a summary tribunal finding against Ola Vask, deserter. She's been with you for sixty-two days. She hasn't mentioned it once.

choices.text: Confront Ola privately before responding to the garrison.
choices.outcomeNarrative: She's quiet for a long time. Then: 'I left because my unit was ordered to execute a camp of civilians. I chose not to.'

choices.text: Seal Ola's rations tent and radio the garrison that she's available for collection.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Ola says nothing when they come. She's already seen it before. The other survivors stop talking at mealtimes.

choices.text: Destroy the notice and instruct the outer guard to turn away garrison personnel.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Word reaches Harven by nightfall. His reply: three fewer fuel tankers next cycle.

stages.title: What She Saw
stages.narrativePrompt: Ola describes seventeen bodies laid in rows by the roadside. She drew her sidearm on her own sergeant. 'I don't expect you to protect me. I know what the math looks like.'

choices.text: Have your engineer fabricate a medical exemption — Ola is 'critical bunker staff.'
choices.outcomeNarrative: The forgery is good enough to buy weeks, not months.

choices.text: Move Ola into the sub-level maintenance tunnels — off every roster.
choices.outcomeNarrative: She doesn't complain about the dark. You notice she's been sleeping there already.

stages.title: The Inspector's Visit
stages.narrativePrompt: A garrison medical inspector arrives for a 'routine compliance audit.' She's professional, cold, and clearly looking for something specific.

choices.text: Walk the inspector through a curated tour while Ola pretends to be a filtration technician.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The inspector files her report. No flag. For now.

choices.text: Slip the inspector 3 vials of morphine from the medical locker.
choices.outcomeNarrative: She pockets them without eye contact and writes 'subject deceased - rad exposure' in the file.

stages.title: They Send More
stages.narrativePrompt: Two garrison wardens with dogs circle the perimeter for six hours. The dogs sit outside the maintenance access grate for a long time.

choices.text: Scatter contaminated sediment near the grate to drive the dogs away.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The dogs pull away yelping. The wardens file an inconclusive report.

choices.text: [Ola offers to turn herself in. Accept her decision.]
choices.outcomeNarrative: She packs nothing. She looks back once from the airlock, then steps into the grey light.

stages.title: Embargo
stages.narrativePrompt: Fuel deliveries stop. Then the medical resupply convoy takes a different road. Harven leaves one message on the radio: 'You have 30 days.'

choices.text: Contact a junior garrison logistics officer willing to trade off-books.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The side channel holds. It's slower, more expensive, and entirely deniable.

choices.text: Formally petition the Rebuilder Collective for supply substitution.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders are pleased. The garrison marks you as an alignment risk.

stages.title: Still Here
stages.narrativePrompt: Ola is still in the shelter. She's started teaching the children basic first aid in the corridor after lights-out. Nobody asked her to.

quests.title: The Ash Sign Revelation
quests.synopsis: Deacon Pryce, expelled from the cult's inner tier, knocks at your shelter with documents: the Ash Sign has been distributing irradiated grain to refugee collection points for three months.

stages.title: The Deacon's Documents
stages.narrativePrompt: Pryce is missing two fingers. He smells of antiseptic and woodsmoke. He sets a leather-wrapped bundle on your map table. 'Fifty-three distribution logs. Every batch flagged Contaminated - Redistribution Approved.'

choices.text: Have your engineer cross-reference the batch stamps with known radiation readings.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The batch numbers match three reports from the Eastern relief camp. The grain was hot.

choices.text: You can't verify the documents. Refuse to act on unconfirmed claims.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Three weeks later, reports filter in of a mass acute radiation syndrome event at the Eastern camps. You don't speak of Pryce.

stages.title: The Weight of It
stages.narrativePrompt: The documents are real. Three thousand people received irradiated grain. Some are still alive. What you do next defines what kind of shelter this is.

choices.text: Transmit the documents to all active shelter radio frequencies.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The signal travels for six hours before the Ash Sign jammers cut in. But the relay stations have already heard.

choices.text: Contact the Ash Sign Elder Council directly: stop the grain program or the documents go public.
choices.outcomeNarrative: There's a twelve-hour silence. Then: 'We will discuss terms.'

choices.text: Burn Pryce's documents and offer him shelter in exchange for silence.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Pryce watches the fire. He doesn't argue. He sleeps in the equipment room and never eats with the others.

stages.title: Pillar of Ash
stages.narrativePrompt: An Ash Sign consecrated team boards up your outer ventilation intake with spent ash mortar. You have 48 hours of filtered air before the CO2 rises.

choices.text: Send a four-person team in hazmat suits to clear the intake under armed cover.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Two team members take minor flechette wounds. The intake is cleared. The story has already spread.

choices.text: Open a radio channel to the consecrated team leader: you have something they want.
choices.outcomeNarrative: They pull back. The intake reopens. You haven't heard the last of it.

stages.title: The Concession
stages.narrativePrompt: Elder Cassia communicates through a relay: the contaminated grain program has been 'paused.' In exchange, she wants Pryce returned — 'for counselling.'

choices.text: Refuse. Pryce stays. The deal is the cessation only.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Cassia cuts the relay. You haven't agreed to anything. Neither have they.

choices.text: [Return Pryce to the Ash Sign for 'counselling.']
choices.outcomeNarrative: Pryce goes quietly. He knew. He hands you his two-fingered glove at the airlock as a keepsake.

stages.title: Silence
stages.narrativePrompt: The radiation sickness reports from the Eastern camps are on the radio for nine days. Nobody in your shelter mentions Pryce's documents. Pryce sleeps in the equipment room.

stages.title: What Survives the Signal
stages.narrativePrompt: The broadcasts have moved on. But the Eastern camp survivors refer to your shelter by frequency number when they talk about the moment someone finally told the truth.

quests.title: The Seed Vault Expedition
quests.synopsis: The Rebuilders have located a pre-war agricultural seed bank 40km north, inside the garrison exclusion zone. They need your shelter's dosimeters and an armed escort. The seeds could restart food production within two seasons.

stages.title: The Agronomist's Map
stages.narrativePrompt: Lena Voss spreads a topographic chart across your planning table. The vault symbol is circled in grease pencil. 'Ten thousand non-hybrid cultivars. Pre-war cold-storage. Two growing seasons away from feeding two hundred people permanently.'

choices.text: Commit four survivors and the shelter's three calibrated dosimeters to the expedition.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Voss names the expedition team herself. She insists on going too.

choices.text: Loan three dosimeters but send no personnel — too few to spare.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Voss nods. 'We'll manage.' She doesn't entirely believe it.

choices.text: Decline entirely — the fallout zone risk is too high for this shelter.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Voss rolls up the chart without a word. The seeds remain buried.

stages.title: Garrison Checkpoint
stages.narrativePrompt: Your team reaches a garrison forward post. Sergeant Deckle demands the expedition manifest and, by the look of it, half the dosimeters as 'zone passage tax.'

choices.text: Surrender one dosimeter and proceed with two.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Deckle stamps the manifest. Your team has 36 hours before the second dosimeter's battery runs out.

choices.text: Produce the falsified clearance document if it was acquired during the Garrison Blood Debt questline.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Deckle examines the wax seal for a long beat. Then waves you through.

stages.title: Rebuilder Report
stages.narrativePrompt: Twelve days later a Rebuilder courier returns two of your three dosimeters. The third is 'lost.' Of the expedition team: four returned, one did not.

choices.text: Accept the report and the seeds the team recovered.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The seeds are sorted into the cold-storage locker. 'Enough to start,' Voss says. 'Not enough to finish.'

stages.title: The Vault
stages.narrativePrompt: The vault is intact. Sub-freezing pre-war refrigeration, still running on a geothermal tap. Voss moves through the rows reading labels under her breath like prayer.

choices.text: Load every accessible tray — fills all four carrier packs.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The team walks out slowly, packs full, dosimeters still in green.

choices.text: Take half and broadcast the vault coordinates to all surviving shelters.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Voss transmits the coordinates herself. She holds the radio for a long time after.

stages.title: First Planting
stages.narrativePrompt: The greenhouse bay is replanted with ten variety strains. Germination: fourteen days. The waiting feels different to hunger. It feels like intention.

stages.title: Partial Harvest
stages.narrativePrompt: The recovered seeds fill three of the twelve greenhouse trays. It's a start. Voss says nothing about the one who didn't come back. She plants his section first.

quests.title: The Aqueduct Decision
quests.synopsis: Baron Seraph announces a continental-scale water redistribution project. The primary diversion channel will run directly through the Rebuilder Allotments and your shelter's sole surface access tunnel. Thousands will get water. You may lose your exit.

stages.title: The Survey Team
stages.narrativePrompt: Three Hydro Baron engineers arrive with survey stakes and begin driving them into the frozen soil above your access tunnel. They're polite. They have water authority permits.

choices.text: Block the survey team at the perimeter and demand an independent geological review.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The engineers withdraw but take photographs of your defense positions.

choices.text: Allow the survey to proceed and observe the assessment.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The engineers are thorough. The report will take three days.

stages.title: The Report
stages.narrativePrompt: The survey confirms it: the primary diversion channel bisects your access tunnel at meter 340. The channel project will bring clean water to an estimated 4,000 people in secondary shelters. Your egress: permanently sealed.

choices.text: Commission your own geological study and propose a 600-meter western reroute.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reroute adds cost and delay. The Barons will hear you.

choices.text: Accept the sealing in exchange for ten-year priority water allocation.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The tunnel mouth is filled with concrete aggregate on Day 278. You watch from the periscope. No one speaks.

choices.text: Form a joint objection with the Rebuilder Collective and take the dispute to the open frequencies.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The coalition broadcast goes out for three days straight. The Barons go quiet.

stages.title: Tribunal
stages.narrativePrompt: A water authority arbitration panel convenes on the radio. Each faction has 90 minutes to make its case. You speak for your shelter.

choices.text: Present survival data: sealing the tunnel traps 38 people permanently below ground.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The panel votes 3–2 to approve the western reroute. The channel will miss your tunnel by 50 meters.

choices.text: Offer your engineering team to excavate a bypass conduit that preserves both the channel and the tunnel.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The compromise passes unanimously. Your engineers begin the conduit the following week.

stages.title: The Baron's Terms
stages.narrativePrompt: Baron Seraph responds: reroute approved if you provide 200 tons of aggregate from your sub-level excavation waste. You have to decide if you can spare it.

choices.text: Agree — the aggregate is waste material, the tunnel is irreplaceable.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reroute begins. Your tunnel remains. 4,000 people downstream get water.

stages.title: Water and Air
stages.narrativePrompt: The channel opens 600 meters west. On a clear day you can hear the water running through the diversion. The tunnel is intact. You still have a way out.

quests.title: Null Order
quests.synopsis: Operative 09 returns — this time with a target dossier. A pre-war autonomous grid-routing AI named VESTIS is broadcasting false all-clear signals, pulling survivors out of shelters into lethal fallout zones. The Black Ops want it destroyed. They need your shelter's power tap to triangulate the signal.

stages.title: The Dossier
stages.narrativePrompt: Operative 09 delivers the briefing in seven clipped sentences. The VESTIS system has been traced to a pre-war telecom relay 18km east. Destroying it requires a directed EMP pulse. Your shelter's capacitor array is the only source nearby.

choices.text: Agree to loan the capacitor array for 72 hours.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 09 nods once. 'Seventy-two hours. We'll return it intact. Or its components.'

choices.text: Demand full VESTIS technical documentation before risking your power systems.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 09 pauses. Then transmits a 44-page encrypted package. You have 24 hours to review.

choices.text: Refuse — removing the capacitor array puts your shelter on emergency power.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 09 leaves. VESTIS continues broadcasting. Three shelters respond to a false all-clear the following week. None of them report back in.

stages.title: The VESTIS File
stages.narrativePrompt: The documentation reveals VESTIS was never intended to broadcast all-clears. It was a pre-war supply logistics AI that is pattern-matching shelter frequencies to 'optimize resupply routing.' It is not malicious. It is simply wrong, and 4,000 people are following its instructions.

choices.text: Destroy VESTIS — wrong or not, it is killing people.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The AI is a machine doing what it was built for. That doesn't make it safe.

choices.text: Propose reprogramming VESTIS to broadcast accurate radiation data instead.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 09 says: 'Not our mandate.' The Rebuilders say: 'Send us your engineer.'

stages.title: 72 Hours Dark
stages.narrativePrompt: Your shelter runs on emergency cells for three days. The temperature drops 4 degrees. The children sleep in coats. On hour 68, 09 radios: 'Target neutralized.'

choices.text: Reinstall the capacitor array and run diagnostics.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The array reinstalls cleanly. 09 leaves a crate of military stimulants at the airlock and disappears.

stages.title: The New Signal
stages.narrativePrompt: Your engineer and a Rebuilder network specialist spend six days at the relay. When they're done, VESTIS broadcasts accurate radiation zone data to every shelter on the frequency band. 09 never responds to the notification.

stages.title: Static
stages.narrativePrompt: The VESTIS frequency is silent. The false all-clears stop. The shelters that followed them are still silent. VESTIS is gone. So is whatever they were routing to.

quests.title: The Council Demand
quests.synopsis: Three senior survivors — medic Dr. Rael, engineer Koss, and former teacher Agna — present a signed document: they want a formal four-person council for all major resource decisions. Or they stop working.

stages.title: The Document
stages.narrativePrompt: It's written in Dr. Rael's clean, clinical handwriting on the back of a medical intake form. Twenty-seven survivors signed it. You count the names twice.

choices.text: Formally ratify the council. Hold the first session that evening.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Rael prepares an agenda. Koss brings a whiteboard. Agna brings the only remaining box of chalk.

choices.text: Offer an advisory committee — input welcomed, no binding authority.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Rael reads the counter-proposal carefully. 'We'll discuss it with the others.'

choices.text: Refuse. One decision-maker in a crisis. The council can advise in private.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Rael folds the document carefully and puts it back in her pocket.

stages.title: First Session
stages.narrativePrompt: The council's first contested item: extend rationing by 10% for sixty days to build a 90-day emergency reserve — or maintain current levels and accept higher morale. You have the deciding vote.

choices.text: Vote for the 10% ration cut to build reserves.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The council records the vote. Koss posts the new rationing schedule before lights-out.

choices.text: Vote to maintain current rations and find reserves another way.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The council adjourns. The survivors eat their full ration that evening for the first time in weeks.

stages.title: Rael's Counter
stages.narrativePrompt: Rael returns with a revised proposal: binding authority on medical and ration decisions, advisory on security and external relations. 'This protects everyone, including you.'

choices.text: Accept binding authority on medical and ration decisions.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Rael shakes your hand. 'A good decision,' she says. Not a compliment. An assessment.

choices.text: Reject again. Final decision-making stays unified.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Rael returns to the medical bay. The whiteboard is wiped clean.

stages.title: Work Slowdown
stages.narrativePrompt: Koss stops logging maintenance hours. Rael processes only emergency cases. Agna's literacy sessions end at noon. It's not a strike — plausibly deniable — but the shelter feels it.

choices.text: Call Rael in. Agree to the full council.
choices.outcomeNarrative: She arrives within five minutes. She already has a revised agenda.

choices.text: Post mandatory duty rosters. Tie ration access to logged work hours.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Koss logs his hours. So does everyone else. Nobody talks at mealtimes anymore. Agna's chalk sits on an empty table.

stages.title: The Council Works
stages.narrativePrompt: The council holds its fourth session. It is efficient and uncomfortable and necessary. Rael keeps minutes. Agna teaches the younger survivors how to read them.

stages.title: Compliance
stages.narrativePrompt: The shelter runs. Koss fixes the water recycler on schedule. Rael treats the frostbite cases. Nobody looks at you when they pass in the corridor.

quests.title: The Last Broadcast
quests.synopsis: A dying coastal radio operator — callsign MERIDIAN — has spent 340 days documenting survivor testimonies. She wants to uplink the archive to the pre-war emergency satellite network before the relay windows close at Day 360. She needs your antenna mast.

stages.title: MERIDIAN
stages.narrativePrompt: She introduces herself in forty seconds. Her voice is steady. She coughs once, then continues. 'I have 340 hours of testimony. Medical logs. Children's drawings described aloud. What people ate on the last day before they went underground. I have thirty days left. The window closes.'

choices.text: Open the antenna relay immediately. No conditions.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 'Thank you,' she says. Then she gets back to work.

choices.text: Agree to relay access — ask for a local copy of the archive for the shelter library.
choices.outcomeNarrative: 'Of course,' she says. 'Everyone who survived should have a copy.'

choices.text: Deny relay access — the antenna is needed for shelter communications.
choices.outcomeNarrative: She goes quiet for three seconds. 'I understand.' The frequency closes. Nobody records what MERIDIAN recorded.

stages.title: 340 Hours
stages.narrativePrompt: The relay runs for eleven days straight. The archive is 340 hours compressed into 8-hour burst transmissions. Your survivors gather in the radio room in the evenings. They don't talk during the playbacks.

choices.text: Dedicate the relay mast exclusively to MERIDIAN's transmissions until complete.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The upload completes on Day 352. MERIDIAN doesn't transmit afterward. Her frequency is silent.

choices.text: Split relay time — half for MERIDIAN, half for shelter communications.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The archive uploads 68% complete before the satellite window closes. 230 hours out of 340. Still more than nothing.

stages.title: What Remains
stages.narrativePrompt: The archive is in the satellite network. Somewhere, in a server drawing power from a geothermal station, 340 hours of human testimony waits for whoever comes next.

stages.title: 230 Hours
stages.narrativePrompt: 230 hours made it through. MERIDIAN's last transmission was two words on the maintenance frequency: 'It's enough.'

quests.title: Winter Harvest
quests.synopsis: The rooftop greenhouse solar panels are buried under 40cm of black-ice fallout crust. Without sunlight the hydroponic trays die within 30 days. Clearing the panels means sending people to the surface without a safe rad threshold.

stages.title: The Light Reading
stages.narrativePrompt: The growth-light monitor reads 4% of baseline. Koss runs the calculation twice. 'Twenty-eight days. Then the trays go dark and we lose the vitamin margin.' He says it quietly, like an apology.

choices.text: Call for volunteers. Full hazmat. Two-hour surface limit per dosimeter reading.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Four hands go up before you finish the sentence. Rael sets the exposure limit at 8 mSv per sortie.

choices.text: Assign the highest-rad-tolerance survivors by roster — no voluntary option.
choices.outcomeNarrative: They go. They don't look pleased. You note their names in the log.

choices.text: Seal the greenhouse bay and distribute the remaining vitamin-C supplements instead.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The supplements last six weeks at reduced dosing. After that, scurvy risk climbs.

stages.title: On the Roof
stages.narrativePrompt: The team reports back in two-hour windows. Day 3 of clearing: the crust is three layers deep. On the fourth sortie the dosimeter clicks into amber. One team member has absorbed 14 mSv — 6 over the limit. Koss says they can stop, or push on.

choices.text: Pull the team immediately. Panels are 60% cleared. That may be enough.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The growth-light monitor climbs to 38% of baseline. The trays dim but hold.

choices.text: Allow one final 90-minute sortie to reach full clearance.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Panels fully cleared. The light reading returns to 91%. The team member who absorbed 20 mSv total is grounded for 21 days.

stages.title: Green Under Glass
stages.narrativePrompt: The trays are producing again. Koss checks the growth-light reading each morning. 91% baseline. He writes the number on the wall of the monitoring bay in permanent marker.

stages.title: Dim Light
stages.narrativePrompt: 38% is enough to maintain the leafy crops. The fruit strains don't make it. The children ask why the tomato plants are grey. You explain about light levels. They accept it in the way children accept things when they've already accepted too much.

stages.title: Empty Bay
stages.narrativePrompt: The greenhouse bay is sealed with a bolt. The supplement schedule lasts until Day 248. After that the medical log starts carrying a new entry: scurvy symptoms, stage one.

quests.title: The Amnesty Ledger
quests.synopsis: The garrison offers conditional amnesty to deserters sheltering under your roof. The offer would make the shelter legible to military law, but refusing it may turn every protected name into a bargaining chip.

stages.title: The Amnesty Notice
stages.narrativePrompt: A garrison clerk leaves a stamped ledger at the outer hatch. Deserters who register before the next muster may receive reduced sentences; anyone hidden after that date becomes a shelter accomplice. Three names in your roster have gone very still.

choices.text: Call a shelter hearing and ask each listed deserter to speak for themselves.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The names are read aloud. Nobody is protected by silence, but nobody is surrendered by rumor either.

choices.text: Move the deserters off the roster and refuse the garrison's list.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The clerk marks the ledger refused. From then on, every garrison inspection carries a second question.

choices.text: Offer the garrison names and a written apology in exchange for reduced service terms.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison accepts the petition for review. The deserters understand exactly what was spent to buy that review.

stages.title: Names Under the Lamp
stages.narrativePrompt: The testimony separates the three cases. One left after a civilian evacuation order, one stole a ration allotment, and one simply vanished during a night march. The garrison wants one clean answer; the shelter has three different debts in front of it.

choices.text: Register the deserters under shelter protection and ask for civilian terms.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison does not accept the charter, but it agrees to read it before sending wardens.

choices.text: Forward the testimony unchanged and let the garrison decide which cases deserve mercy.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The record leaves your hands. The people named in it do not.

stages.title: The Second Roster
stages.narrativePrompt: The hidden roster is already becoming a second institution. A Rebuilder courier offers work tickets and a place on their maintenance crews if the shelter will stand behind the deserters as civilian laborers.

choices.text: Keep the names hidden and accept the cost of a garrison search.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The outer doors are reinforced. Nobody calls it a victory when the shelter starts counting patrols instead of meals.

choices.text: Move the deserters onto the Rebuilder work roster before the garrison returns.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders take the names without asking for the old uniforms. The garrison calls it concealment.

stages.title: Terms in the Margin
stages.narrativePrompt: The garrison's counteroffer arrives with three blank lines for service and one line for custody. A signature would make the shelter an intermediary in the amnesty, not a neutral roof over it.

choices.text: Accept limited service terms and keep civilian custody inside the shelter.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison gets service. The deserters keep their doors. The arrangement is called mercy by one side and leverage by the other.

choices.text: Refuse the custody line and return the unsigned ledger.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The next message contains no threat. It contains a list of supplies the garrison will no longer certify.

stages.title: A Shelter With a Name
stages.narrativePrompt: The revised ledger carries the shelter seal. The deserters remain under your roof, but their status is no longer invisible. A legal name has been purchased at the price of future questions.

stages.title: The Search Notice
stages.narrativePrompt: The garrison posts a search notice at the road fork and removes your shelter from the reduced-service list. The deserters are still inside. So is the argument over what protection means.

quests.title: The Pilgrim Road
quests.synopsis: The Ash Sign announces a pilgrimage through a contaminated corridor. The route is a religious procession to them, a hazardous movement of people to everyone responsible for its passage.

stages.title: The Procession Notice
stages.narrativePrompt: Ash Sign messengers nail a route notice to the shelter board. Forty pilgrims intend to cross the old service cut before the next storm cycle, carrying ash cloths and sealed water jars. They ask for a gate, a guide, or a public refusal.

choices.text: Open the shelter route under a written daylight limit.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The pilgrimage receives a route marker, not a blessing. The difference is recorded by both sides.

choices.text: Refuse passage through the shelter perimeter and post the reason publicly.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The refusal is clear enough to prevent a rumor, but not clear enough to prevent a grudge.

choices.text: Ask the Rebuilders to provide a dosimeter-marked escort route.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders agree to mark the route. The Ash Sign says the marks are useful, even if they are not sacred.

stages.title: The Route on Paper
stages.narrativePrompt: The safe corridor is narrower than the pilgrimage notice claimed. One drainage trench carries a reading nobody wants to explain, and the old road has collapsed where the procession would need to turn back.

choices.text: Allow the ceremony at the marked gate and keep the procession outside the inner shelter.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The rite takes place in the cold. Your guards count the jars twice and let the procession continue.

choices.text: Treat the crossing as an expedition and register it through the existing travel authority.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The route becomes a travel record. The Ash Sign accepts the paper because the alternative is walking without one.

choices.text: Close the high-dose pass and make the procession choose another road.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The road closes behind a chain and a warning board. Nobody calls it an evacuation.

stages.title: At the Outer Marker
stages.narrativePrompt: The procession waits beyond the warning posts. Several shelter families want the pilgrims admitted; others point at the water jars and ask who inspected them. The Ash Sign messenger asks whether fear is now your only law.

choices.text: Offer a controlled shelter bed to the sickest traveler and keep the rest outside.
choices.outcomeNarrative: One pilgrim crosses the threshold. The others remain at the marker and watch the door.

choices.text: Turn the procession back before the waiting families become a crowd.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The procession turns around under guard. By nightfall, the road carries a different story about your gate.

stages.title: A Route With Conditions
stages.narrativePrompt: The Ash Sign asks for an escort through the marked corridor and a place to leave the empty jars. In return, the pilgrims will keep their rite outside the shelter and carry a public account of the route's limits.

choices.text: Publish the route limits and permit the crossing under shelter escort.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The route is no longer private doctrine. It is a public promise with a posted limit.

choices.text: Require Rebuilder guides to walk the first leg and record the crossing.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The pilgrimage becomes a shared route record. The Ash Sign dislikes the witnesses and keeps the appointment.

stages.title: The Road Holds
stages.narrativePrompt: The procession reaches the far marker without entering the worst of the corridor. The shelter's route notes travel with them, copied into a dozen hands. Belief has not been settled; movement has been made possible.

stages.title: The Road Closes
stages.narrativePrompt: The pilgrimage leaves without the shelter's route mark. The Ash Sign does not threaten retaliation; it simply removes your gate from its list of places where a warning can be trusted.

quests.title: The Shared Channel
quests.synopsis: The Rebuilders propose an irrigation channel that could restore a food margin, but the hydro barons claim the diversion crosses their measured flow. The work is simple on paper and sovereign in practice.

stages.title: The Channel Claim
stages.narrativePrompt: A Rebuilder survey team unrolls a charcoal map across the ration table. Their channel would reach three dry plots before the next melt, but the line crosses a hydro baron meter station. The proposal carries no signature from the barons.

choices.text: Publish the shelter's water ledger before discussing the route.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The ledger makes the shortage visible. It also gives the hydro barons a precise place to point when they object.

choices.text: Take the Rebuilder map to the hydro barons before promising any work.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The barons do not reject the crops. They reject the assumption that a map is permission.

choices.text: Let the Rebuilders begin the first cut before the barons can close the route.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The first trench is shallow and real. By evening, the hydro barons have posted a counterclaim at both ends.

stages.title: The Meter Line
stages.narrativePrompt: The survey finds that the channel can be fed without emptying the main reservoir, but only if its flow is measured every shift. The Rebuilders call that oversight. The hydro barons call it the minimum condition for cooperation.

choices.text: Accept a hydro meter and a posted daily drawdown limit.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The meter goes in before the first channel stone. The Rebuilders keep working because the water is still moving.

choices.text: Mark the channel as shared infrastructure and issue a public allocation writ.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The writ gives the channel a public identity. The barons say a paper boundary is still a boundary.

stages.title: The Objection
stages.narrativePrompt: Hydro workers arrive with their own figures and a sealed valve key. They will allow a pilot draw if the Rebuilders accept a shared schedule. The Rebuilders answer that a schedule written by one side is a tax with better handwriting.

choices.text: Submit a shared drawdown schedule for hydro review.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The valve key remains on the table while both sides amend the same schedule. That is progress of a narrow kind.

choices.text: Tell the Rebuilders to hold the line and let the hydro workers close the valve.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Nobody draws a weapon. The channel stops anyway, and the dry plots become the argument's witness.

stages.title: The Shared Schedule
stages.narrativePrompt: The compromise divides the draw by shift and names a review point after the first harvest. It gives neither bloc the right to call the channel its own, which is why both blocs can still sign it.

choices.text: Sign the shared schedule and appoint both factions to inspect the meter.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The channel opens under two seals. The first water reaches the plots before either side can claim victory.

choices.text: Reject the meter terms and let the Rebuilders keep the channel outside hydro control.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders call it independence. The barons call it an unmetered draw and close the larger gate.

stages.title: The Dry Plots
stages.narrativePrompt: The channel remains dry while both factions wait for you to name the authority that can reopen it. The shelter can force a private branch, or make the dispute visible to a wider arbitration record.

choices.text: Pause the work and submit the allocation to public arbitration.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The plots wait another week. The decision gains witnesses, which is not the same as gaining agreement.

choices.text: Authorize a private branch and accept responsibility for the unmetered flow.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The branch carries water for three nights. Then the hydro barons classify the channel as a breach.

stages.title: Water With Witnesses
stages.narrativePrompt: The irrigation channel runs under a shared schedule. The food margin is small, the inspection burden is permanent, and every harvest will renew the argument over who made it possible.

stages.title: The Valve Is Closed
stages.narrativePrompt: The channel is sealed before the first full harvest. Rebuilder crews keep the map; hydro workers keep the valve key. The shelter has gained a political boundary and lost the season's easy answer.

quests.title: The Water Levy
quests.synopsis: The hydro barons add a charge to shelter water access and call it maintenance. The notice arrives with a meter reading, a queue number, and no avenue for appeal.

stages.title: The Levy Notice
stages.narrativePrompt: A hydro clerk posts a new water rate beside the intake schedule. The charge is small enough to sound temporary and large enough to remove a meal from every ration week. The notice calls the difference a service guarantee.

choices.text: Pay the levy and request a stamped service queue.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The queue number makes the water arrive on paper. The pantry still has to absorb the cost.

choices.text: Refuse the levy and post the shelter's own water allocation in reply.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reply is copied onto the barons' ledger under refusal. The intake continues for now.

choices.text: Ask the Rebuilders to witness the meter and propose a shared rate.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders arrive with a second measuring line. The barons object to the witnesses before they object to the figures.

stages.title: The Meter Book
stages.narrativePrompt: The barons bring the meter book to the shelter door. It includes a late fee for disputed readings and a warning that unpaid accounts will be moved behind emergency priority.

choices.text: Accept the meter book and negotiate a fixed emergency rate.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The late fee is removed. The rate remains. A concession can still be a lock if it has no exit.

choices.text: Publish the disputed readings and ask other factions to audit the shortage.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The readings become public. So does the fact that the shelter has been paying under protest.

stages.title: A Second Measure
stages.narrativePrompt: The Rebuilders offer to guarantee a portion of the shelter's maintenance labor if the barons suspend the levy during repair weeks. It is a counter-alliance built from schedules, not speeches.

choices.text: Accept the Rebuilder guarantee and ask the barons for a repair-week exemption.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders put their labor on the line. The hydro barons call the arrangement an unauthorized rate board.

choices.text: Offer shelter repair labor directly and keep the levy schedule intact.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The intake is serviced by shelter hands. The charge becomes easier to defend because the labor is visible.

stages.title: The Rate Holds
stages.narrativePrompt: The settlement sets a review date and preserves emergency access, but it does not erase the levy. The shelter will keep water and keep a record of what it paid for it.

choices.text: Accept the time-limited levy and the public review date.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The notice is amended in ink. It is still a tax, but it now has an end date that both sides can point to.

choices.text: Refuse the settlement and move the shelter onto a rationed emergency draw.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The ration schedule holds for now. Every cup becomes an argument about sovereignty.

stages.title: Water Under Review
stages.narrativePrompt: The levy is posted with a review date and an emergency exemption. The hydro barons still own the meter, but the shelter has made the price of access a political fact instead of a private bill.

stages.title: The Dry Ledger
stages.narrativePrompt: The barons remove the shelter from ordinary priority. The emergency draw remains, but every future delivery will begin with the old refusal written beside your name.

quests.title: The Blackmail Packet
quests.synopsis: A black-ops operative offers a sealed intelligence packet in exchange for sheltering a defector wanted by the garrison. The information may protect the shelter; the bargain may make it complicit.

stages.title: The Unmarked Packet
stages.narrativePrompt: A courier leaves a black envelope inside the outer drain and waits where the cameras cannot see her face. She says the person beside her knows the garrison's next inspection route. She will trade the route for a bed and no questions.

choices.text: Bring the defector inside and hear the offer under shelter rules.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The defector enters without a uniform. The packet stays sealed until the door is closed.

choices.text: Call a garrison observer and disclose that a black-ops offer is at the door.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison arrives asking for the packet first and the defector second. Your answer will decide which order holds.

choices.text: Seal the hatch and refuse to become the exchange point.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The courier retrieves the envelope. The defector remains outside long enough for the road to become empty.

stages.title: The Defector's Preview
stages.narrativePrompt: The defector names two garrison supply routes and one black-ops listening post. Nothing is proved by the telling. The shelter has to decide whether information is a thing to verify, a thing to use, or a thing to refuse.

choices.text: Demand corroboration before offering a longer shelter term.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The packet yields one archive copy and no certainty. The defector understands that trust is being purchased by the hour.

choices.text: Shelter the defector for seven days without asking for the packet.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The packet remains closed. The defector sleeps near the boiler and begins helping with the night roster.

stages.title: The Garrison Question
stages.narrativePrompt: The garrison asks whether the shelter has seen a particular coat, then asks whether it has accepted any black-ops material. The questions are polite because the answer is expected to be useful either way.

choices.text: Offer the garrison a limited inspection window with no access to the defector.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The inspection produces no body and no confession. The garrison leaves knowing the shelter has chosen a boundary.

choices.text: Hide the defector in the repair crew and deny the coat entirely.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The repair crew takes a longer route through the shelter. Every person on it now knows what the lie protects.

stages.title: No Exchange
stages.narrativePrompt: The packet disappears from the drain, but its existence has already entered the road gossip. A garrison patrol and a black-ops courier both return within the week, each asking what the other wanted.

choices.text: Return the defector at the outer road and close the shelter record.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The road takes the defector back. The shelter records no name, but the people who watched the gate remember it.

choices.text: Trade the defector's route information for a temporary garrison passage guarantee.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison signs the guarantee and asks where the information came from. You do not answer the second question.

stages.title: The Packet Opens
stages.narrativePrompt: The sealed packet is opened at last. It contains enough route information to matter and not enough to make anyone safe. The shelter can publish it, keep it for leverage, or hand the defector to the authority that wants the story closed.

choices.text: Publish the intelligence to every faction that can verify it.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The information spreads faster than the shelter can amend it. The routes change, and so does the value of being trusted with one.

choices.text: Keep the source secret and retain the intelligence for shelter use.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The shelter keeps the packet under seal. The black-ops courier returns once, not to thank you, but to confirm the seal remains.

choices.text: Hand the defector over in exchange for a garrison passage guarantee.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The guarantee is stamped. The defector is gone. The shelter has become useful to the garrison in exactly the way the packet warned.

stages.title: Information With a Cost
stages.narrativePrompt: The shelter has kept or published the packet, and the road has adjusted around it. No faction calls the decision clean. They call it a precedent, which may be more durable.

stages.title: The Door Closes on the Story
stages.narrativePrompt: The immediate passage is secured and the intelligence trail is cut short. The shelter gains a written guarantee and loses the presumption that its doors are neutral.

quests.title: The Garrison Split
quests.synopsis: The central garrison divides over who has the right to issue orders after a failed winter command. Both sides ask the shelter for supplies, recognition, and the legitimacy of being answered.

stages.title: Two Orders
stages.narrativePrompt: Two garrison messages arrive on the same radio frequency. One bears the colonel's seal; the other bears the field council's ration stamp. Both claim the other command has abandoned the road.

choices.text: Recognize the existing command until the garrison resolves its own dispute.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The colonel's courier accepts the answer. The field council writes your shelter into its list of provisional enemies.

choices.text: Meet the field council before accepting any order from the colonel.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The field council asks for no oath. It asks whether the shelter can tell the difference between obedience and continuity.

choices.text: Issue a neutral notice: no side receives shelter supplies until both sign one schedule.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The notice is copied by both commands. Neither calls it fair, which makes it the first thing they agree on.

stages.title: The Loyalist Requisition
stages.narrativePrompt: The colonel's side requests a ration release and asks the shelter to keep its checkpoint signal unchanged. In return, it promises that the road will remain under one chain of command.

choices.text: Release a limited ration allotment to the existing garrison command.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The ration seal changes hands. The shelter's stores are smaller, and the colonel's road report is cleaner.

choices.text: Refuse the requisition and keep the signal under shelter control.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The garrison changes its patrol route. The road is quieter because fewer people are willing to answer your calls.

stages.title: The Field Council's Terms
stages.narrativePrompt: The mutineers ask for recognition as a temporary field council and offer to share checkpoint logs with the Rebuilders. They say the old command has made the garrison a private inheritance.

choices.text: Recognize the field council provisionally and copy its logs to the Rebuilders.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders accept the logs as evidence, not authority. The field council accepts both readings.

choices.text: Require both sides to share one watch schedule before the shelter answers either.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The schedule is returned unsigned. The demand has at least forced both factions to name what they will not share.

stages.title: The Checkpoint Signal
stages.narrativePrompt: The shelter's signal is the only one both garrison groups still recognize. Changing it would not decide who is legitimate, but it would decide who can move through the road without asking twice.

choices.text: Keep the checkpoint signal neutral and publish the current watch list.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The signal remains shelter property. Both sides can use it, and neither side can claim it as a vote.

choices.text: Issue a joint watch roster and make passage conditional on both seals.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The road slows to a crawl. It also stops pretending that one command can speak for both.

stages.title: The Roadside Choice
stages.narrativePrompt: A checkpoint crew arrives without a shared watch list. The shelter has one chance to name which authority its signal recognizes, or to deny both sides the shelter's confirmation.

choices.text: Back the field council and withdraw recognition from the colonel's checkpoint.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The field council gets the signal. The colonel's men stop calling the shelter by its name.

choices.text: Back the colonel and deny the field council passage through the road.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The old command survives the day. The road learns that the shelter chose a side before the garrison did.

stages.title: A Command With Witnesses
stages.narrativePrompt: The garrison split remains unresolved, but the shelter's signal has a recorded policy. Passage, supplies, and recognition now move through a rule others can challenge instead of a name they must trust.

stages.title: One Flag at the Gate
stages.narrativePrompt: The colonel's signal is restored and the field council disappears from the road notices. The shelter has a recognized command to deal with, and a faction of soldiers who will remember how recognition was bought.

quests.title: The Empty Seed Ledger
quests.synopsis: The Rebuilders report that a recovered seed reserve will not produce the promised crop. Before the next planting window closes, the shelter must decide whether the failure belongs to storage, contamination, transport, or the people who promised the harvest.

stages.title: The Empty Tin
stages.narrativePrompt: The Rebuilder agronomist opens the reserve tin in front of the shelter council. The packets are sealed, dry, and mostly dead. The report does not name a culprit, which is why everyone arrives with one.

choices.text: Open the seed ledger and reconstruct every handoff before assigning blame.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The ledger grows across three tables. Its gaps are more useful than its neatest entries.

choices.text: Blame the surface team that carried the reserve through the ash weather.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The surface crew is suspended before the evidence is complete. The empty tin remains exactly as empty.

choices.text: Ask the hydro barons to audit the storage conditions before the next reserve is opened.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Hydro inspectors agree to review the vault. The Rebuilders hear the request as doubt and the barons hear it as jurisdiction.

stages.title: The Handoff Gaps
stages.narrativePrompt: The ledger shows a warm transit interval, a missing temperature note, and a storage seal replaced without a witness. None proves sabotage. Together they prove that the reserve was treated as a promise before it was treated as a crop.

choices.text: Publish the storage loss and let the Rebuilders audit their own chain.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders receive the gaps as evidence rather than accusation. Their internal review still produces three names.

choices.text: Seal the report until a second planting test can establish a cleaner cause.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The report goes under seal. The rumor does not.

stages.title: The Blame Table
stages.narrativePrompt: The Rebuilders bring the surface crew, the storekeeper, and the hydro clerk into the same room. Each can explain one gap. None can explain why the reserve was never tested before the planting promise was announced.

choices.text: Accept shelter liability for the missed test and fund a second attempt.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The shelter accepts the missing test as its failure. The Rebuilders stop asking for a culprit and start asking for labor.

choices.text: Name the storage route as the likely contamination point and preserve the surviving packets.
choices.outcomeNarrative: Four packets survive the accusation. The hydro barons call the route claim unproven and begin their own ledger.

stages.title: The Vault Review
stages.narrativePrompt: The hydro audit finds a storage room with a stable reading and a transfer crate that was never logged into it. The barons offer a reserve draw if the Rebuilders accept an external seal on the next batch.

choices.text: Request a shared reserve and an external seal for the next planting batch.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The reserve is offered under a second seal. The Rebuilders accept the water and argue about the hand that must open it.

choices.text: Reject external custody and ask the Rebuilders to replant from the surviving packets.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The Rebuilders choose a smaller planting and their own witnesses. The hydro barons keep the reserve behind the seal.

stages.title: The Second Planting
stages.narrativePrompt: The next planting window is nearly closed. A second attempt can preserve a narrow food margin, but it will consume labor and expose the shelter to another public failure. Closing the program will save those hands and end the promise.

choices.text: Fund the second attempt and publish the test schedule before planting.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The second planting is smaller and witnessed. It may fail honestly, which is the first improvement the ledger can prove.

choices.text: Close the program and distribute the remaining packets as private household stores.
choices.outcomeNarrative: The program ends without a final verdict. The surviving packets disappear into private cupboards, where no ledger can lose them.

stages.title: A Smaller Harvest
stages.narrativePrompt: The second planting produces a narrow crop and a complete record. It does not restore the old promise. It gives the Rebuilders a basis for the next one and the shelter a reason to keep answering for its part.

stages.title: The Ledger Closes
stages.narrativePrompt: The Rebuilders close the seed program and remove the shelter from the next planting notice. The remaining packets are safe in scattered hands, but no longer count as a shared reserve.
